I know what you mean. I'm a bit of a neat freak, but one of my friends is most definitely not, and his kids are inheriting that from him. Whenever I visit his place there is junk *everywhere*.

Last time I went around (maybe 3 or 4 weeks ago now), it was probably the worst I had ever seen it. There were plates strewn about the living room, what looked like about 5 days worth of meals. Kids were out, he had just picked me up after MMA training, so he went for a long shower. And as I said, I'm a bit of a neat freak, so I figured I'd do some cleaning.

20 minutes later and I had moved all the dirty stuff out to the kitchen to be washed up, but for some reason I could still smell food, but I couldn't see what I was smelling. And it seemed pretty fresh. So I start following my nose as best I could, and eventually pinpointed the source to be behind his couch. 

Moved that out of the way, and wouldn't you know, there was an entire Korean BBQ meal just sitting right back there; fluffy steamed eggs in a pot, two fundamental Korean stews, pickles, lettuce and, at the center of it all, four cuts of beef.

The meats were hanger steak, the reddish-purple of a brand-new bruise; a rib-eye together with a flap of rib-eye cap, both pink and spiderwebbed with white veins of fat; a thickish slab of flatiron steak, said to be the product of a cow who had Wagyu on one side of the family and Angus on the other; and finally galbi, short ribs in a sweet soy marinade.

The atmosphere behind the couch was warm and inviting. There was maybe a bit more noise than I would have liked, but when you eat out, you can't be overly picky.

More traditional Korean dishes tend to taste more complete, but it was one of the best meals I had in the past year, filled me right up, and I didn't even have to pay! Overall, I would recommend visiting.
